reasoning: Recent Maine Senate polling in the last 45 days shows a very close race, with the most recent public polls generally putting Democrat Troy Jackson a few points ahead of Republican Susan Collins, while an average/forecast source still has Collins narrowly ahead. Because the latest state-specific polls are within or near the margin of error and point to a slight Democratic edge, the current race margin is best described as roughly D+3 to D+4, though the state remains effectively a toss-up.

sources.name: The Hill / University of New Hampshire Poll
sources.details: University of New Hampshire poll of likely general-election voters found Troy Jackson ahead of Susan Collins 49% to 46%.

sources.name: Spectrum News / University of New Hampshire Poll
sources.details: University of New Hampshire poll reported Jackson leading Collins 49% to 46%, a three-point Democratic edge.

sources.name: The Maine Wire / Hart Research Poll
sources.details: Hart Research poll for the Senate Majority PAC found Jackson leading Collins 49% to 45% among likely voters.

sources.name: Bangor Daily News / Hart Research Poll
sources.details: Reported the Hart Research poll showing Jackson up 49% to 45% and noted that a previous UNH poll also had Jackson ahead.

sources.name: Pollsmax Maine Senate Forecast
sources.details: Polling-average/forecast page shows Collins ahead 48.5% to 45.4%, which is a 3.1-point Republican edge, but this is an aggregator rather than a fresh state poll.
